There are 60 minutes in an hour.

Regarding the competitor's strategy, Streamline Autos' direct-to-consumer (DTC) model for electric vehicles presents a significant challenge to traditional automotive sales structures. By bypassing dealerships, they reduce overhead costs, allowing for more competitive pricing that could attract price-sensitive consumers. This shift not only disrupts the established dealership network but also gives Streamline Autos direct access to customer data, enabling them to refine their products and marketing in real-time based on actual consumer behavior.

For our business, this implies a need to reassess our own sales and distribution channels. If we rely heavily on traditional dealership partnerships, we may face margin pressure and slower feedback loops compared to Streamline Autos. To remain competitive, we might consider integrating more direct digital engagement tools, enhancing our online sales capabilities, or leveraging our existing dealer network to offer superior value-added services that a pure DTC model cannot easily replicate. Additionally, investing in data analytics to better understand customer preferences will be crucial to counter their informational advantage.
